jobs.description:
Now with a $2,000 sign-on bonus for new Seneca employees!

Ready to turn meaningful relationships into lasting impact? As the Director of Development
to our Northern California region you will be responsible for developing and implementing strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward donors in support of the agency’s mission. You will play a key role in strengthening and growing our community of supporters while working alongside a supportive and inclusive team. This position focuses on securing gifts by building long-term relationships with a diverse constituency, including individuals, corporate and institutional donors capable of making significant philanthropic investments. Bring your passion for fundraising and help shape the future of our organization, join our team today!

Seneca
has been nominated among the Bay Area’s Top Workplaces for several consecutive years. We’re committed to providing traditionally marginalized communities with a network of excellent mental health, community-based, and educational services. We are committed to building a diverse staff. Our programs deeply engage in conversations and training on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion to bring equity and justice to the youth and families we serve.

Major Gifts Program Implementation

Execute a comprehensive, strategic, donor-centered major gifts program in the Bay Area and throughout Northern California that includes specific fundraising goals and targets, with a focus on acquisition of leadership gifts ($10,000+ annually) from high level prospects and donors
Understand Seneca’s programs, priority initiatives, goals and financial needs to develop compelling cases for support that inspire leadership giving across diverse communities, with a focus on attracting new prospective donors to the work

Prepare regular fundraising and regional activity reports for senior leadership and the board

Portfolio Management

Develop and manage a portfolio of approximately 100 current donors and prospects giving or capable of giving $10,000+ annually, including individual, corporate and institutional funders
Identify, engage, inspire and build relationships with all assigned donors through personalized, meaningful and timely engagement, outreach, site visits, donor meetings, proposals, and events
Support effective prospecting to identify and research current donors and new prospects with capacity and inclination to make annual gifts of $10,000 or more
Collaborate with cross-functional colleagues, both with Development department and enterprise colleagues, for coordinated donor outreach, stewardship reports, and impact communications
Maintain effective Moves Management through accurate and timely recording of donor interactions, planned future engagement and gift opportunities in Raisers Edge
Analyze portfolio performance, monitor progress toward goals, and prepare regular reports for senior management
Support campaign planning and execution, including setting and tracking goals
Identify and cultivate planned giving prospects to secure long-term philanthropic support

Required

Master's degree OR Bachelor's degree

Minimum of 4 years of progressive fundraising experience and demonstrated success in independently and collaboratively prospecting, cultivating, soliciting, and successfully closing donor gifts

jobs.title: Chief Communications Officer
jobs.description:
Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory invites visionary communications leaders to apply for the role of Chief Communications Officer
(CCO)—an opportunity to shape the voice and reputation of one of the world's premier scientific research institutions. The CCO will lead Berkeley Lab's strategic communications function and help advance the Laboratory's mission of delivering science solutions to the world's greatest challenges.

Reporting directly to the Laboratory Director and serving as a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief Communications Officer is a trusted strategic advisor who partners with senior leaders to advance Berkeley Lab's scientific, operational, fiscal, cultural, and reputational goals. Leading the 17-person Strategic Communications Office, the CCO will develop and execute a bold, integrated communications strategy that elevates the Laboratory's global profile, strengthens engagement with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), the University of California (UC), policymakers, scientific collaborators, employees, and surrounding communities, and reinforces Berkeley Lab's position as a world leader in scientific innovation.

This role leads a modern, Lab-wide communications organization, inspires a high-performing team, and shapes compelling narratives that showcase groundbreaking research, operational excellence, organizational culture, and public impact. The successful candidate will foster trust across diverse stakeholders, lead through moments of opportunity and complexity, and ensure Berkeley Lab's voice reflects its enduring commitment to scientific excellence, innovation, service, and stewardship.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Institutional Strategy
Develop and execute an enterprise-wide communications strategy aligned with the Laboratory’s scientific mission, strategic priorities, and reputation, with clear outcomes and data analytics to evaluate progress, including the impacts of AI on stakeholder information gathering.
Advise the Laboratory Director and executive leadership on reputation, issues management, stakeholder engagement, and institutional positioning.
Translate long-term institutional vision into actionable communication strategies that advance scientific leadership and programmatic ambitions across internal and external audiences.
Drive integrated storytelling across programs and directorates to reinforce a unified Laboratory identity.

Science Communication & Impact
Position the Laboratory as a global leader in science, innovation, and impact.
Lead communications across the Lab’s research portfolio in energy, computation, artificial intelligence, quantum, materials, biological sciences, and related disciplines.
Proactively engage national and global media to elevate the Laboratory’s reputation for scientific excellence and impact.
Connect programmatic priorities to broader societal challenges to strengthen understanding of federally funded science and its value.
Direct a modern digital and media ecosystem aligned with audience expectations and institutional storytelling needs.

Internal Communications, Culture & Engagement
Lead a Lab-wide internal communications program that fosters shared purpose across a complex organization with multiple internal communities.
Partner with Lab leaders to communicate a culture grounded in stewardship, shared values, and safety.
Work with functional areas (e.g., the Stewardship Office and Human Resources) to communicate organizational change in ways that build trust and engagement.
Strengthen cohesion across research and operations communications teams to support execution of Laboratory priorities.
Lead internal efforts to execute programs that foster employee engagement.

Crisis & Emergency Communications
Prepare for and lead emergency and crisis communications that protect people, assets and reputation while maintaining and building stakeholder trust.
Advise senior leadership in real time during high-consequence crises, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and institutional credibility.
Be available after hours and on weekends to advise and lead crisis communications as needed.

Stakeholder Engagement & Relationship Building
Build trust and alignment across stakeholder communities through clear, consistent, and responsive messaging.
Serve as the senior communications interface with DOE, UC,, the State of California, academic partners, industry, and local communities.
Coordinate communications across national laboratory peers (the National Laboratories Chief Communications Officers) and research partners to reinforce mission alignment and collective impact.
Represent the Laboratory in national forums where communications, science policy, and institutional reputation converge.

Organizational Leadership & Team Development
Strengthen integration across decentralized communications teams to lead a cohesive, Lab-wide communications enterprise, leveraging distributed expertise into a unified strategic function.
Foster a high-performing communications culture grounded in collaboration, trust, accountability, innovation, and excellence.
Oversee budgeting, workforce planning, and resource allocation for Strategic Communications, aligned with institutional priorities.
Anticipate and adapt to shifts in the information landscape, including misinformation, evolving practices, and AI-enabled tools and workflows.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic communications, public affairs, or related fields, ideally within a science-driven, research, academic, government, or similarly complex institutional environment.

Strategic Communications Leadership
Proven ability to design and execute enterprise-scale, integrated communications strategies aligned with institutional mission, scientific leadership, and long-term programmatic priorities in large, distributed organizations.
Record of advising senior executives on reputation, issues management, and strategic messaging.
Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills with deep fluency in modern practices across digital, media, internal communications, branding, and executive messaging.

Stakeholder Relationships
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across complex stakeholder ecosystems, including federal agencies, academic partners, and public-sector institutions.
Ability to balance diverse and sometimes competing stakeholder needs while maintaining institutional coherence and credibility.
High emotional intelligence, sound judgment, and credibility at all levels, with the ability to influence without authority and build trust across scientific, operational, and executive communities.

Crisis, Risk & Reputation Management
Significant experience leading crisis and emergency communications, operating effectively under pressure while maintaining transparency and alignment with institutional values.
Proven ability to protect institutional reputation while sustaining trust with internal and external stakeholders.

Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness
Proven success in leading and developing high-performing, multidisciplinary teams.
Experience driving organizational alignment, cross-functional collaboration, and institutional change in complex environments.
Strong budgeting, operational planning, and resource management skills.

Desired Qualifications:

Advanced degree (Master's or Ph.D.) in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field.
Experience leading communications activities in a DOE national laboratory or FFRDC environment.
Familiarity with data-informed communications approaches and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools and workflows.

Application Guidelines:

Please submit your CV and letter of interest by September 7, 2026,
for priority consideration. Applications will be accepted until the job posting is removed.
In the cover letter, please highlight (i) your interest in the position, (ii) relevant organizational leadership experience, and (iii) most notable accomplishments.

Notes:

Appointment type:
This is a full-time career appointment, exempt from overtime pay (monthly paid). The Chief Communications Officer position is appointed by and serves at the discretion of the Laboratory Director, and this appointment is at will and may be terminated at any time with or without cause.
Salary range:
This position is expected to pay $290,000 to $360,000 annually; salary will be commensurate with the final candidate’s qualification and experience, including skills, knowledge, relevant education, certifications, as well as aligned with the internal leadership peer group. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position.
Background check:
This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
Work modality:
This position requires daily on-site presence at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA, with occasional business travel.

Koniag IT Systems Inc, a Koniag Government Services company, is seeking an experienced Senior Program Director to lead a large-scale, mission-critical enterprise communications and IT services program supporting Department of War installations in the Colorado Springs, CO area. This is for a future new business opportunity.

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) retirement plan, paid time off, paid parental leave, life and disability insurance, flexible spending accounts, commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement.

This role is responsible for executing a zero-fail phase-in of legacy contract requirements, standing up unified service delivery across multiple installations, and driving cybersecurity, quality, and operational excellence across a workforce of approximately 400 technical personnel. The ideal candidate is a seasoned program leader with deep experience in DoW, AirForce and Space Force IT/communications operations, fixed-price contract management, and complex workforce transitions, who can operate confidently at the executive level with Government stakeholders up to GO/SES equivalent. An active Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility is required. This position is on-site in Colorado Springs, CO, with routine travel among Peterson SFB, Schriever SFB, Cheyenne Mountain SFS, and associated GSUs, and requires availability for on-call support outside normal duty hours.

Responsibilities

The Senior Program Director will serve as the single point of accountability for planning, executing, and sustaining a large, multi-site enterprise communications and IT services program in a mission-critical, no-fail environment. This individual will lead the full lifecycle of program execution — from phase-in and workforce transition through steady-state service delivery, compliance, and continuous improvement. Principal responsibilities will include but are not limited to:

Enterprise & Workforce Transition (Zero-Failure)

Own and execute the phase-in plan across 60–90 day transition windows for each legacy requirement, sequencing acceptance of O&M responsibility so no work center experiences a service gap.
Lead recruiting, hiring, clearance processing, badging, base/restricted-area access, and onboarding of approximately 400 technical personnel under tight, overlapping timelines; manage incumbent capture and right-of-first-refusal considerations alongside external hiring pipelines.
Drive clearance velocity as a schedule-critical path item (Secret through TS/SCI, NC2 packets, SCI nomination letters, Entry Access Letters) in partnership with corporate FSO, the SSO, and program security staff.
Own structured incumbent knowledge capture for legacy and end-of-life mission systems, historical architectures, and cable plant documentation; convert tacit knowledge into transferable procedures before legacy contracts expire.
Forge a unified operational culture across the incoming contractor workforce, enduring government civilian communications specialists, mission partners, and Base Infrastructure Modernization (BIM) interfaces.

Unified Service Delivery & Operations

Stand up and govern a consolidated, standardized, scalable Communications Focal Point / service desk capable of absorbing enterprise ticket volumes and differentiating support across N/NC, Mission, and AFNET networks.
Establish major-incident management capability for events such as mass network isolation, including surge staffing models, automated remediation alternatives to manual software reinstallation, and clear prioritization rules.
Institute a synchronized reporting framework across Technical Control Facilities (TCFs) and work centers that gives Government leadership a real-time common operating picture during critical outages.
Maintain accountability for 24x7x365 coverage, mission-essential and exercise support, VIP/executive communications, and life-safety systems including Giant Voice and external emergency notification interfaces.

Cybersecurity, Compliance & Quality

Own a scalable, integrated cybersecurity framework covering EMSEC/TEMPEST documentation verification, RMF packages and ATO timelines, continuous configuration monitoring, vulnerability management, privileged access management, and COMSEC.
Ensure proactive compliance with AFCYBER TASKORDs, DoD 8140 workforce qualification, CMMC requirements, and applicable AFIs/DAFMANs; eliminate EMSEC and configuration backlogs that delay secure system deployment.
Own the Quality Control Plan and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) interface, performance metrics and SLAs, CDRL deliverables (including the Program Management Plan), contractor manpower reporting, and Quarterly Program Management Reviews.
Build an internal, repeatable training and certification program that sustains workforce readiness and breaks the entry-level "revolving door" turnover pattern in call center, help desk, and client systems roles.

Legacy & Mission Systems Sustainment

Ensure sustainment, troubleshooting, and configuration management for specialized and legacy mission systems and dependent analog endpoints (fire alarms, gate intercoms, public address, DRSN, PNVC, LMR, FAB-T support), including obsolescence and parts-availability risk mitigation.
Manage touch maintenance, logistics, IT asset management, Equipment Control Officer/property custodian functions, software license management, and technology refresh planning across all three installations.
Oversee confined space, PDS walks, PMI, MEP, and cable installation/maintenance activities with full safety and OSHA/AFOSH compliance.

Governance, Innovation & Business Performance

Enforce configuration management protocols, contractual boundaries, and government oversight; prevent unauthorized network alterations and unilateral decision-making by mission partners or subcontractors.
Provide immediate (within 15 minutes) notification to the GPM of any issue affecting performance, and disciplined scope control for work the company considers outside contract scope.
Deliver fixed-price financial performance: staffing models, indirect and subcontract management, CLIN execution, travel and local purchase controls, and margin protection under a firm-fixed-price structure.
Lead teaming and subcontractor integration under an 8(a) prime arrangement, including partner performance, workshare, and flow-down compliance.
Champion continuous improvement and innovation — automation, intelligent service management tooling, and data-driven service delivery — moving the enterprise from reactive sustainment to proactive, resilient operations.

Required

Education and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, information systems, business, or a related field.
Minimum 15 years of progressive program/project management experience on DoW IT, communications, or base operating support contracts, including at least 10 years as PM or Deputy PM of record.
Demonstrated experience managing a services program of at least $25M annual value and 150+ personnel; experience at 400+ personnel scale strongly preferred.

Demonstrated fixed-price contract P&L management, EVM or equivalent cost/schedule control, and CDRL/QASP performance reporting.

jobs.description:
About the Organization

Short Summary
Pursuit is a pioneering AI-native organization building the nation's premier tech workforce pipeline to unlock lasting economic mobility for low-income and underrepresented communities.

Long Summary
For over a decade, Pursuit has unlocked economic mobility by propelling thousands of adults from low-income backgrounds into high-wage tech careers, taking average starting incomes from $17K to $94K and generating nearly $1B in lifetime wage gains. We've also pioneered the Pursuit Bond, an innovative outcomes-based financing model that aligns investor returns with long-term economic mobility, allowing us to scale impact in a financially sustainable way.
Now, as AI reshapes the global economy, Pursuit is pioneering the nation's premier AI-Native workforce pipeline. We are transforming how economic opportunity works at scale through a rigorous, full-funnel training model combining in-person collaborative learning, real-time curriculum adaptation, and deep employer integration.
Powered by $20M in scale funding from organizations like Google, Anthropic, Adobe, Blackstone, Robin Hood and others, Pursuit is building a roadmap of growth to directly train thousands of more Americans and to build enduring workforce training solutions that can support the ecosystem at large.

About the Position

What You'll Do

As Pursuit scales its AI-Native workforce model and launches in early 2027 the New York AI Jobs Institute (AIJI)—our new premier NYC institute backed by $13M in public funding to unite leaders across government, industry, and education to train millions of residents for AI careers—we are strengthening our operational infrastructure to match our accelerating impact. We are seeking a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to serve as our chief architect of operational excellence. Reporting directly to the CEO, this leader will be a central pillar of the executive leadership team, driving strategic decision-making and actively shaping the future of Pursuit's training programs and job placement initiatives. While managing the finance, operations, and people functions, they will architect the foundational systems required to scale our mission and impact.
Beyond executive strategy, as a true strategic partner to the CEO, the COO will translate organizational vision into high-performing infrastructure—architecting the KPIs, dashboards, and organizational systems that power our next phase of scale.. More than building systems, they will cultivate a culture of accountability and high performance, aligning elite teams around shared standards while fiercely protecting the values that brought us here. This is a rare opportunity for a transformative leader to elevate an organization at a defining inflection point.

Key responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Organizational Leadership and Performance Excellence

Serve as key organizational leader who helps lead strategic decisions and embeds operational rigor and accelerates enterprise-wide execution across all functions and in particular, Program, Go-To-Market Job Placement, Partnerships, Growth and Earned Revenue .
Serve as the executive architect of organizational performance, establishing the enterprise metrics, dashboards, and analytical systems that guide executive decision-making and Board governance.
Design and maintain the dashboards and KPI architecture that give the CEO, leadership team, and Board a real-time, accurate view of organizational health.
Spearhead the optimization of Pursuit's internal infrastructure, scaling the tools, workflows, and AI-native processes necessary for rapid, sustainable growth
Establish robust performance management systems and accountability structures that empower elite teams to excel.

Organizational Design & Scale

Architect Pursuit's evolving organizational structure, designing reporting lines and team topologies intentionally aligned with our forward-looking strategy rather than historical growth.
Partner with the CEO and other leaders on enterprise-wide workforce planning, capacity building, and talent scaling.
Establish robust change management strategies and cross-functional collaboration frameworks to ensure seamless organizational transitions as Pursuit scales its impact.

Business Operations

Exercise executive ownership over all business operations, unifying finance, HR, talent, culture, and core organizational workflows into a seamlessly integrated operational backbone.
Provide direct managerial leadership and oversight to the VP of Finance and VP of People, guiding their strategic direction and aligning team priorities with enterprise goals.
Drive financial leadership in partnership with the VP of Finance, overseeing multi-year budgeting, resource allocation, financial modeling, and sound fiscal governance across all departments.
Champion talent acquisition, HR infrastructure, and human capital strategy alongside the VP of People to attract, retain, and develop world-class teams.
Cultivate and safeguard Pursuit's organizational culture, fostering an environment of accountability, continuous learning, high performance, and mission alignment.
Oversee core operational processes, facilities management, internal systems, and revenue collections (including the Pursuit Bond) to scale efficiency as the organization grows.

Who You'll Work With

You will report to the Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the executive team you will be a key strategic shaper of the future and optimization of every function at Pursuit — Program, Go-To-Market Job Placement, Partnerships, Growth and Earned Revenue. You will directly manage the VP of Finance, VP of People, General Counsel, Head of AI implementation, Head of Facilities and Operations and more.

Required Skills and Experience

8–12 years of experience in business operations or leadership operations roles, ideally spanning both a strategy/consulting environment and a hands-on operating role inside a growing company or organization.
Previous consultative experience (e.g., management consulting or a similar advisory background), paired with real experience actually running operations, not just advising on them.
Exceptional analytical and strategic thinking skills with experience leading or partnering closely with strategic finance functions
A history of cultivating elite teams and establishing high-performance standards amidst rapid organizational scaling.
Demonstrated success and track-record in architecting robust operational systems, processes, and infrastructure that drive enterprise-wide execution and long-term quality.
Extensive experience designing and governing executive-level KPI frameworks, real-time dashboards, and strategic reporting systems for complex, fast-growing organizations.
Deep expertise in organizational design, structural transformation, and team topology scaling to align operational architecture with long-term enterprise strategy.
Experience building or running business operations and HR/People systems and practices at scale.
High tolerance for ambiguity and bias toward building, comfortable creating structure where none exists yet.
Deeply motivated by Pursuit's mission of economic transformation and expanded opportunity for low-income and underrepresented communities.
MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $300,000 - $330,000, inclusive of base and bonus and a full benefits package.
The compensation above reflects the expectations laid out in this job description; however, we are often open to a wide variety of profiles and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this posting. If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated to you as a candidate.

Additional Details

Location and Work Environment

This role is based in NYC. Pursuit currently operates on a hybrid schedule, Tuesday through Thursday on-site at our office in New York City,, with a Monday/Friday work-from-anywhere policy.

Benefits

Full benefits package including vision and dental
Unlimited PTO, plus an all-Pursuit summer break (last week of August) and a week-long holiday break (last week of December)
401k match
Hybrid and flexible work policy, as described above
Dedicated time to build in AI and develop your own AI skills

Equity at Pursuit

We prioritize the richness of diversity across all categories. We welcome new perspectives and make employment decisions without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, age, familial or marital status, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory invites visionary communications leaders to apply for the role of Chief Communications Officer
(CCO)—an opportunity to shape the voice and reputation of one of the world's premier scientific research institutions. The CCO will lead Berkeley Lab's strategic communications function and help advance the Laboratory's mission of delivering science solutions to the world's greatest challenges.

Reporting directly to the Laboratory Director and serving as a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief Communications Officer is a trusted strategic advisor who partners with senior leaders to advance Berkeley Lab's scientific, operational, fiscal, cultural, and reputational goals. Leading the 17-person Strategic Communications Office, the CCO will develop and execute a bold, integrated communications strategy that elevates the Laboratory's global profile, strengthens engagement with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), the University of California (UC), policymakers, scientific collaborators, employees, and surrounding communities, and reinforces Berkeley Lab's position as a world leader in scientific innovation.

This role leads a modern, Lab-wide communications organization, inspires a high-performing team, and shapes compelling narratives that showcase groundbreaking research, operational excellence, organizational culture, and public impact. The successful candidate will foster trust across diverse stakeholders, lead through moments of opportunity and complexity, and ensure Berkeley Lab's voice reflects its enduring commitment to scientific excellence, innovation, service, and stewardship.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Institutional Strategy
Develop and execute an enterprise-wide communications strategy aligned with the Laboratory’s scientific mission, strategic priorities, and reputation, with clear outcomes and data analytics to evaluate progress, including the impacts of AI on stakeholder information gathering.
Advise the Laboratory Director and executive leadership on reputation, issues management, stakeholder engagement, and institutional positioning.
Translate long-term institutional vision into actionable communication strategies that advance scientific leadership and programmatic ambitions across internal and external audiences.
Drive integrated storytelling across programs and directorates to reinforce a unified Laboratory identity.

Science Communication & Impact
Position the Laboratory as a global leader in science, innovation, and impact.
Lead communications across the Lab’s research portfolio in energy, computation, artificial intelligence, quantum, materials, biological sciences, and related disciplines.
Proactively engage national and global media to elevate the Laboratory’s reputation for scientific excellence and impact.
Connect programmatic priorities to broader societal challenges to strengthen understanding of federally funded science and its value.
Direct a modern digital and media ecosystem aligned with audience expectations and institutional storytelling needs.

Internal Communications, Culture & Engagement
Lead a Lab-wide internal communications program that fosters shared purpose across a complex organization with multiple internal communities.
Partner with Lab leaders to communicate a culture grounded in stewardship, shared values, and safety.
Work with functional areas (e.g., the Stewardship Office and Human Resources) to communicate organizational change in ways that build trust and engagement.
Strengthen cohesion across research and operations communications teams to support execution of Laboratory priorities.
Lead internal efforts to execute programs that foster employee engagement.

Crisis & Emergency Communications
Prepare for and lead emergency and crisis communications that protect people, assets and reputation while maintaining and building stakeholder trust.
Advise senior leadership in real time during high-consequence crises, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and institutional credibility.
Be available after hours and on weekends to advise and lead crisis communications as needed.

Stakeholder Engagement & Relationship Building
Build trust and alignment across stakeholder communities through clear, consistent, and responsive messaging.
Serve as the senior communications interface with DOE, UC,, the State of California, academic partners, industry, and local communities.
Coordinate communications across national laboratory peers (the National Laboratories Chief Communications Officers) and research partners to reinforce mission alignment and collective impact.
Represent the Laboratory in national forums where communications, science policy, and institutional reputation converge.

Organizational Leadership & Team Development
Strengthen integration across decentralized communications teams to lead a cohesive, Lab-wide communications enterprise, leveraging distributed expertise into a unified strategic function.
Foster a high-performing communications culture grounded in collaboration, trust, accountability, innovation, and excellence.
Oversee budgeting, workforce planning, and resource allocation for Strategic Communications, aligned with institutional priorities.
Anticipate and adapt to shifts in the information landscape, including misinformation, evolving practices, and AI-enabled tools and workflows.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in strategic communications, public affairs, or related fields, ideally within a science-driven, research, academic, government, or similarly complex institutional environment.

Strategic Communications Leadership
Proven ability to design and execute enterprise-scale, integrated communications strategies aligned with institutional mission, scientific leadership, and long-term programmatic priorities in large, distributed organizations.
Record of advising senior executives on reputation, issues management, and strategic messaging.
Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills with deep fluency in modern practices across digital, media, internal communications, branding, and executive messaging.

Stakeholder Relationships
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across complex stakeholder ecosystems, including federal agencies, academic partners, and public-sector institutions.
Ability to balance diverse and sometimes competing stakeholder needs while maintaining institutional coherence and credibility.
High emotional intelligence, sound judgment, and credibility at all levels, with the ability to influence without authority and build trust across scientific, operational, and executive communities.

Crisis, Risk & Reputation Management
Significant experience leading crisis and emergency communications, operating effectively under pressure while maintaining transparency and alignment with institutional values.
Proven ability to protect institutional reputation while sustaining trust with internal and external stakeholders.

Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness
Proven success in leading and developing high-performing, multidisciplinary teams.
Experience driving organizational alignment, cross-functional collaboration, and institutional change in complex environments.
Strong budgeting, operational planning, and resource management skills.

Desired Qualifications:

Advanced degree (Master's or Ph.D.) in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing, or a related field.
Experience leading communications activities in a DOE national laboratory or FFRDC environment.
Familiarity with data-informed communications approaches and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools and workflows.

Application Guidelines:

Please submit your CV and letter of interest by September 7, 2026,
for priority consideration. Applications will be accepted until the job posting is removed.
In the cover letter, please highlight (i) your interest in the position, (ii) relevant organizational leadership experience, and (iii) most notable accomplishments.

Notes:

Appointment type:
This is a full-time career appointment, exempt from overtime pay (monthly paid). The Chief Communications Officer position is appointed by and serves at the discretion of the Laboratory Director, and this appointment is at will and may be terminated at any time with or without cause.
Salary range:
This position is expected to pay $290,000 to $360,000 annually; salary will be commensurate with the final candidate’s qualification and experience, including skills, knowledge, relevant education, certifications, as well as aligned with the internal leadership peer group. It is not typical for an individual to be offered a salary at or near the top of the range for a position.
Background check:
This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.
Work modality:
This position requires daily on-site presence at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA, with occasional business travel.

About the Organization

Short Summary
Pursuit is a pioneering AI-native organization building the nation's premier tech workforce pipeline to unlock lasting economic mobility for low-income and underrepresented communities.

Long Summary
For over a decade, Pursuit has unlocked economic mobility by propelling thousands of adults from low-income backgrounds into high-wage tech careers, taking average starting incomes from $17K to $94K and generating nearly $1B in lifetime wage gains. We've also pioneered the Pursuit Bond, an innovative outcomes-based financing model that aligns investor returns with long-term economic mobility, allowing us to scale impact in a financially sustainable way.
Now, as AI reshapes the global economy, Pursuit is pioneering the nation's premier AI-Native workforce pipeline. We are transforming how economic opportunity works at scale through a rigorous, full-funnel training model combining in-person collaborative learning, real-time curriculum adaptation, and deep employer integration.
Powered by $20M in scale funding from organizations like Google, Anthropic, Adobe, Blackstone, Robin Hood and others, Pursuit is building a roadmap of growth to directly train thousands of more Americans and to build enduring workforce training solutions that can support the ecosystem at large.

About the Position

What You'll Do

As Pursuit scales its AI-Native workforce model and launches in early 2027 the New York AI Jobs Institute (AIJI)—our new premier NYC institute backed by $13M in public funding to unite leaders across government, industry, and education to train millions of residents for AI careers—we are strengthening our operational infrastructure to match our accelerating impact. We are seeking a Chief Operating Officer (COO) to serve as our chief architect of operational excellence. Reporting directly to the CEO, this leader will be a central pillar of the executive leadership team, driving strategic decision-making and actively shaping the future of Pursuit's training programs and job placement initiatives. While managing the finance, operations, and people functions, they will architect the foundational systems required to scale our mission and impact.
Beyond executive strategy, as a true strategic partner to the CEO, the COO will translate organizational vision into high-performing infrastructure—architecting the KPIs, dashboards, and organizational systems that power our next phase of scale.. More than building systems, they will cultivate a culture of accountability and high performance, aligning elite teams around shared standards while fiercely protecting the values that brought us here. This is a rare opportunity for a transformative leader to elevate an organization at a defining inflection point.

Key responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Organizational Leadership and Performance Excellence

Serve as key organizational leader who helps lead strategic decisions and embeds operational rigor and accelerates enterprise-wide execution across all functions and in particular, Program, Go-To-Market Job Placement, Partnerships, Growth and Earned Revenue .
Serve as the executive architect of organizational performance, establishing the enterprise metrics, dashboards, and analytical systems that guide executive decision-making and Board governance.
Design and maintain the dashboards and KPI architecture that give the CEO, leadership team, and Board a real-time, accurate view of organizational health.
Spearhead the optimization of Pursuit's internal infrastructure, scaling the tools, workflows, and AI-native processes necessary for rapid, sustainable growth
Establish robust performance management systems and accountability structures that empower elite teams to excel.

Organizational Design & Scale

Architect Pursuit's evolving organizational structure, designing reporting lines and team topologies intentionally aligned with our forward-looking strategy rather than historical growth.
Partner with the CEO and other leaders on enterprise-wide workforce planning, capacity building, and talent scaling.
Establish robust change management strategies and cross-functional collaboration frameworks to ensure seamless organizational transitions as Pursuit scales its impact.

Business Operations

Exercise executive ownership over all business operations, unifying finance, HR, talent, culture, and core organizational workflows into a seamlessly integrated operational backbone.
Provide direct managerial leadership and oversight to the VP of Finance and VP of People, guiding their strategic direction and aligning team priorities with enterprise goals.
Drive financial leadership in partnership with the VP of Finance, overseeing multi-year budgeting, resource allocation, financial modeling, and sound fiscal governance across all departments.
Champion talent acquisition, HR infrastructure, and human capital strategy alongside the VP of People to attract, retain, and develop world-class teams.
Cultivate and safeguard Pursuit's organizational culture, fostering an environment of accountability, continuous learning, high performance, and mission alignment.
Oversee core operational processes, facilities management, internal systems, and revenue collections (including the Pursuit Bond) to scale efficiency as the organization grows.

Who You'll Work With

You will report to the Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the executive team you will be a key strategic shaper of the future and optimization of every function at Pursuit — Program, Go-To-Market Job Placement, Partnerships, Growth and Earned Revenue. You will directly manage the VP of Finance, VP of People, General Counsel, Head of AI implementation, Head of Facilities and Operations and more.

Required Skills and Experience

8–12 years of experience in business operations or leadership operations roles, ideally spanning both a strategy/consulting environment and a hands-on operating role inside a growing company or organization.
Previous consultative experience (e.g., management consulting or a similar advisory background), paired with real experience actually running operations, not just advising on them.
Exceptional analytical and strategic thinking skills with experience leading or partnering closely with strategic finance functions
A history of cultivating elite teams and establishing high-performance standards amidst rapid organizational scaling.
Demonstrated success and track-record in architecting robust operational systems, processes, and infrastructure that drive enterprise-wide execution and long-term quality.
Extensive experience designing and governing executive-level KPI frameworks, real-time dashboards, and strategic reporting systems for complex, fast-growing organizations.
Deep expertise in organizational design, structural transformation, and team topology scaling to align operational architecture with long-term enterprise strategy.
Experience building or running business operations and HR/People systems and practices at scale.
High tolerance for ambiguity and bias toward building, comfortable creating structure where none exists yet.
Deeply motivated by Pursuit's mission of economic transformation and expanded opportunity for low-income and underrepresented communities.
MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is $300,000 - $330,000, inclusive of base and bonus and a full benefits package.
The compensation above reflects the expectations laid out in this job description; however, we are often open to a wide variety of profiles and recognize that the person we hire may be less experienced (or more senior) than this posting. If that ends up being the case, the updated salary range will be communicated to you as a candidate.

Additional Details

Location and Work Environment

This role is based in NYC. Pursuit currently operates on a hybrid schedule, Tuesday through Thursday on-site at our office in New York City,, with a Monday/Friday work-from-anywhere policy.

Benefits

Full benefits package including vision and dental
Unlimited PTO, plus an all-Pursuit summer break (last week of August) and a week-long holiday break (last week of December)
401k match
Hybrid and flexible work policy, as described above
Dedicated time to build in AI and develop your own AI skills

Equity at Pursuit

We welcome new perspectives and make employment decisions without regard to race, color, ancestry, religion, national origin, age, familial or marital status, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law.
